title: Hourglass sprint tally — personal probe log
content:
Quick summary:
- Personal tracking sheet for a short burst of microbench runs (hourglass sprint).
- Goal: compare small-batch inference latency and token cost across 3 quant profiles while keeping per-request latency under 120ms P95 where possible.
- Rough checklist: capture P50/P95, memory OOMs, model output sanity for 512/1024 seq lengths, annotate bad samples.

Notes to self (short):
- Keep warmup runs separate; ignore first 10 tokens for P50.
- Use same prompt seed for sanity checks.
- If output quality drops (hallucination), mark run as BAD and note sample ids.

Runs (compact table, personal shorthand):
ID | model | quant | batch | seq | p50(ms) | p95(ms) | cost/1k | mem | verdict | notes
---|-------|-------|-------|-----|---------|---------|--------|-----|--------|------
R1 | llama-13b | a8x | 1 | 512 | 38 | 96 | $0.26 | 11.2G | ok | slight tensor-sum slowdown after 300 toks
R2 | llama-13b | fp16 | 1 | 512 | 44 | 110 | $0.38 | 15.8G | ok | higher mem but cleaner tokens
R3 | llama-13b | a4 | 2 | 512 | 55 | 160 | $0.18 | 10.9G | warn | p95 > 120ms, occasional odd token truncation
R4 | redwood-13b-v2 | a8x | 1 | 1024 | 72 | 185 | $0.40 | 12.4G | bad | OOM spike in run 4b, need to repro with trace
R5 | redwood-13b-v2 | q4_0 | 1 | 512 | 34 | 88 | $0.20 | 9.6G | ok | best cost/latency balance so far

Quick impressions:
- a8x quant seems promising for 512-seq single-batch; keeps p50 low.
- q4_0 is cost-effective and stable — annotate as candidate for canary.
- a4 with batch=2 can reduce unit cost but loses tail latency; not acceptable for low-latency endpoints.
- redwood-13b-v2 OOM on 1024: need to capture kernel trace and cf-run id.

Action items / next steps:
- [ ] Re-run R4 with memory profiler + capture nvtx (ticket JIRA-ML-3421).
- [ ] Add 3 deterministic prompts to sanity set and run diff-checker to flag hallucinations.
- [ ] Try burst mode warmup (10 back-to-back requests) vs steady warmup; compare p95 delta.
- [ ] Push candidate config (model redwood-13b-v2 q4_0, batch=1) to canary route and run 24h sample.

Scratchpad / ad-hoc notes:
- Might try prefix caching for 512 prompts to see if p95 improves for a4 batch=2 case.
- Remember to set telemetry tag: "hourglass-sprint/2026-02" on runs for easier filtering.
- Link to quick eval harness: small-eval/README in my fork (local).

Sample flagged tokens (for manual review):
- R3 sample s_091: output ended with repeated token sequence ("the the the").
- R4b trace id: trace-20260218-9efc (need to pull logs).

Loose heuristics I used here (personal):
- p50 under 50ms = great for single-turn chat.
- p95 under 120ms = acceptable for low-latency product paths.
- cost/1k threshold $0.30 = try to be under for scale.

End of sheet. This is intentionally compact — move stable variant notes to a product brief once candidate is selected.

References / quick links:
- Confluence: /display/INF/Low+Latency+Canary (bookmark)
- GitHub PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/serving-runtime/pull/879
- Jira: JIRA-ML-3421 (OOM investigation)

-- Anika
